title: lore sync has no fail-closed option when log regeneration would drop unrecognized content
description:
`lore sync` regenerates `docs/log.md` as a MERGE (LCLI-485): committed entries the visible git
history can no longer account for are carried forward, and every line that is neither structure nor
a legible entry is counted into `LogMergeStats.dropped` and reported as a warning. That warning is
deliberately emitted before the write and on `--dry-run` too. It is the right behaviour for an
operator watching a terminal.

IT IS THE WRONG BEHAVIOUR FOR AN UNATTENDED RUN, which is the request. A warning is a signal that
requires a reader. A CI job, a scheduled sync, or an agent loop has none: the run exits 0, the drop
is real, and the loss is discovered later in a diff someone thinks to take. Wanted: an OPT-IN option
that makes `lore sync` REFUSE BEFORE ANY WRITES when regeneration would drop unrecognized log
content. Default behaviour (warn, proceed, exit 0) must not change -- this is fail-closed as a
choice, not a new default.

PROVENANCE: downstream validation feedback on the published lore 0.6.2 / quest 0.6.2 pair, from host
mbpm2, which runs a real integration consumer against the published CLIs. 2026-09-14. Their 0.6.2
run PASSED -- 99 repository workflow tests, zero skips, and lore's history preservation, drop
warnings, accounting, dry-run and `--no-index` behaviour all passed. They flagged this EXPLICITLY as
a feature suggestion, not a failed fix and not a regression. Evidence at
`results/analysis/proof-graph-pilot-20260913/build-validation/lore-quest-0.6.2-20260914/validation-report.md`
on mbpm2; ask them rather than guessing at their setup if more detail is needed.

WHERE THE CODE IS, verified 2026-09-14 on dev at 661529cf, not inferred:

- `src/core/log.ts` -- `generateLogWithStats` / `LogMergeStats`. `dropped` is the count,
  `droppedSamples` is up to DROPPED_SAMPLE_LIMIT (3) of the lines verbatim, bounded on purpose.
- `src/commands/sync.ts:241` -- `if (regenerated !== undefined && regenerated.log.dropped > 0)`
  builds `droppedContentWarning` and flushes it.

THE CHECK POINT ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY IN THE RIGHT PLACE, which is what makes this small.
`regenerateIndexAndLog` STAGES into the `writes` map; it does not write. The whole write phase --
the symlink preflight, `writeManyAtomicOrRollback`, and `sweepTrackerStorage` -- is gated behind the
`if (!parsed.dryRun)` blocks that FOLLOW the warning at line 241. So a refusal thrown where the
warning is built is structurally before every docs write and before the tracker sweep.

"BEFORE ANY WRITES" IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST BE PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. A guard that aborts halfway has
already done damage. The one thing I did NOT verify is whether `gatherReconciliation`'s Backlog
round-trip can itself mutate anything before line 241 is reached. Establish that rather than
reasoning from the function's name.

SURFACE IS AN OPEN DECISION, and both arms are defensible: a flag (`--fail-on-drop`, explicit at the
call site, trivially greppable in a CI file) or a `.lore/config.toml` setting (applies to every sync
in a repository without every caller remembering, which is closer to what an unattended workflow
actually wants). Doing both is legitimate. Whoever takes it should decide and say why.

INTERACTIONS TO SETTLE: `--no-index` skips regeneration entirely (`regenerated` is undefined), so
there is nothing to refuse -- decide whether combining it with the guard is a silent no-op or a
usage error. `--dry-run` already writes nothing, so the guard there is purely about the exit code,
and a nonzero exit from a dry run is arguably exactly what an unattended pre-check wants.

WIDER POINT, recorded because it is why this is worth more than its size: we have spent a great deal
of effort this month on gates that reported and passed. This is a user asking for the fail-closed
variant of exactly that, and they are right to want it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An opt-in option makes `lore sync` exit nonzero and write NOTHING when log regeneration would drop unrecognized lines. Default behaviour -- warn, proceed, exit 0 -- is unchanged, and a test proves the default still passes.

The refusal is proven to happen before ANY write by a test that asserts the on-disk bytes of docs/ AND the tracker storage are byte-identical to before the run -- not merely that the exit code was nonzero. `gatherReconciliation`'s pre-warning Backlog round-trip is established to be non-mutating rather than assumed to be.

The refusal message names what would be dropped -- the count and the bounded `droppedSamples` the existing warning already carries -- so an unattended runner's captured log is enough to act on without re-running interactively.
The exit code is an existing documented `LoreError` type already in sync's manifest `exitCodes`, not a new bare number, and the manifest entry for sync describes the new surface.

The `--no-index` and `--dry-run` interactions are decided, documented and tested: `--no-index` performs no regeneration so there is nothing to refuse, and `--dry-run` writes nothing so the guard there is purely an exit code.
The chosen surface -- flag, `.lore/config.toml` setting, or both -- is recorded WITH ITS REASON, and appears in both `lore sync --help` and `lore manifest --json`.
`bun run lint`, `typecheck` and the test suite pass, and `lore check` exits 0.

plan: Add an opt-in --fail-on-drop flag to lore sync: manifest flag entry (drives parsing, help and the machine manifest), a drift LoreError thrown at the existing LCLI-485 drop-warning site in src/commands/sync.ts, and a usage error for --fail-on-drop --no-index.

Prove the refusal is pre-write against on-disk bytes: snapshot the whole repo tree (docs/ + tracker storage) across a refusal, in both a fake-seam and a real-git fixture, each paired with the same fixture run without the flag as a control.
implementationNotes: SURFACE DECIDED: a flag (--fail-on-drop), NOT a .lore/config.toml setting, and not both. Reason, recorded in the src/commands/sync.ts module header so it lives with the code: the guard changes a run's outcome, and sync's documented default is 'warn and proceed'. A repository-wide setting would make an interactive lore sync exit 6 for a reason invisible at the call site, and would then need an inverse flag to escape for a single run -- two new surfaces, where the unattended callers who asked for this already pass flags explicitly in a CI file where '--fail-on-drop' greps. A secondary, honest input: the config surface's tests live in test/config.test.ts, which was outside this agent's assigned file scope, so a config setting would have shipped less tested than the flag.

EXIT CODE: drift (exit 6), an existing LoreError type already in sync's manifest exitCodes [0,2,3,4,5,6] -- asserted in the test against findManifestCommand('sync').exitCodes rather than against a literal. Grounding: cli-contract 4.1 says a warning changes the exit code precisely when the command is a defined gate for that condition, which is what --fail-on-drop opts the run into being; 5.3's 'drift' is the category for on-disk bytes a lore generator can no longer account for. 'denied' (4) was the other candidate and was rejected: it is already what the read/write seams return for EACCES here, so it would not be distinguishable.

INTERACTIONS DECIDED. --no-index + --fail-on-drop is a fail-loud usage error (exit 2), raised in parseSyncArgs before the bundle is even loaded -- NOT a silent no-op. --no-index skips log regeneration entirely, so the guard can never fire, and accepting the pair would leave a CI file reading as protection while providing none: the exact 'reported and passed' shape this flag exists to remove. --dry-run + --fail-on-drop still refuses (exit 6) and is deliberately not a conflict: a dry run writes nothing either way, so the guard there is purely the exit code, which is how an unattended job asks 'would a real sync lose anything?' without touching the tree. The refusal message says 'would drop' unconditionally -- a refused run never writes, so the warning's indicative 'drops' is never true under the flag.

THE CRUX -- is anything before sync.ts's drop-warning site mutating? ESTABLISHED, two ways, not assumed. (1) Statically, over the whole pre-warning call path: loadProfile, loadBundle, scopeConcepts, linkedConcepts, readReconcileConfig (loadConfig + adapter.statusFlow/pausedStatus), validateReconcileInputs, gatherReconciliation, readSource, regenerateIndexAndLog (readIndexBytes, generateIndexes, orphanedIndexPaths, readFileIfPresent, resolveHeadSha, realGitAdapter). A grep for writeFile/writeFileSync/mkdirSync/rmSync/renameSync/appendFile/Bun.write/unlinkSync across every module in that path (core/bundle, core/profile, config, core/indexes, core/log, commands/discover, adapters/git, core/reconcile, core/managed-block, core/concept, adapters/tracker, adapters/backlog, adapters/quest) returns exactly ONE hit: adapters/backlog.ts's bunBacklogSpawn mkdtempSync's a throwaway isolation directory under the system tmpdir and rmSync's it in a finally -- outside the repository either way. regenerateIndexAndLog stages into the writes map and writes nothing. The tracker subcommands the round-trip issues are reads: backlog --version, task list --json, task view --json, plus a readStatusFlow file read; quest --version, task status-flow --json, task view --json. (2) Empirically, by the two byte-snapshot tests in the next note. RESIDUAL GAP, stated plainly: what a third-party quest/backlog BINARY does inside its own storage while serving a read subcommand is not provable from this repository, and the byte-snapshot tests use the in-memory fake adapter, so no real tracker subprocess is exercised by them. That gap is identical for every other lore command and is not specific to this change.

ON-DISK-BYTES PROOF (the AC's requirement that this not be an exit-code assertion). Two tests in test/sync.test.ts snapshot every file under the repo root -- docs/ AND backlog/ AND .lore/ -- as path->bytes, run the refusal, and assert byte-identity. (a) 'writes NOTHING: every byte under the repo root survives the refusal, and the tracker sweep never runs' uses the fake seams and also asserts the recording GitSpawn's .calls is empty, so sweepTrackerStorage demonstrably never ran. (b) 'real git: no docs write, no lore-authored backlog/ commit, identical working tree' uses a real repository with realGitAdapter, resolveHeadSha and bunGitSpawn, and also asserts that rev-list --count HEAD and status --porcelain are unchanged. Each pairs the refusal with the SAME fixture run WITHOUT the flag, asserting the tree does change and a commit is made -- a snapshot comparison over a fixture that would not have written anything anyway proves nothing, so the control is load-bearing. The fixture is one where an ordinary sync genuinely writes: a linked Story whose task is now Done (status rewrite plus managed-block regen), no index.md yet (a creation), a log.md carrying two lines of prose (a rewrite plus the drop), and a dirty tracker storage directory for the sweep.

MUTATION TESTING -- every new test was proven able to fail by breaking the behaviour it covers, then the source was restored from a backup copy and the suite re-verified green. M1 guard never fires (if (false)): 4 fail -- both refusal tests and both byte-snapshot tests. M2 guard MOVED to after the write phase and the tracker sweep, the mutation that matters because it is a guard aborting too late: 3 fail, caught by the tree snapshot (its diff showed docs/index.md and docs/stories/index.md created and log.md rewritten) and by the log.md byte assertion; the --dry-run test correctly still PASSED, since a dry run writes nothing either way. M3 error type drift to denied: 2 fail. M4 --no-index conflict check removed: 1 fail (the usage test). M5 droppedSamples removed from the refusal message and input: 1 fail (the AC#3 assertion). M6 guard ignores the flag (if (true)), i.e. the default changes: 6 fail, including the new default-unchanged test, both controls, and three pre-existing LCLI-485 warning tests. M7 manifest flag summary loses the phrase 'before any write': 1 fail (the help/manifest test).

COMMAND OUTPUT, run on feat/LCLI-492-fail-on-drop in an isolated worktree. bun run lint: exit 0, 235 files checked, 1 warning -- PRE-EXISTING, src/commands/agents.ts:216 useOptionalChain, present before this change and outside the assigned scope. bun run typecheck: exit 0 (tsc --noEmit plus tsconfig.scripts.json). bun run src/cli.ts check: exit 0, 77 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 9 out-of-bundle links skipped. bun test: 2995 tests across 95 files, 2993 pass, 1 skip, 1 fail, 1 error -- the fail and the error are both test/ladybug-version-qualification.test.ts, which reads join(root, 'node_modules', '@ladybugdb', 'core', 'package.json') and ENOENTs because this worktree has no node_modules of its own (module resolution walks up to the primary checkout, but that hardcoded path does not). Unrelated to this change and expected to pass in the primary checkout; worth re-running there before treating the suite as green. test/sync.test.ts alone: 53 pass, 0 fail, 232 expect() calls, of which 8 tests are new here.

SCOPE BOUNDARY, for whoever lands this. docs/reference/cli-surface.md's sync entry still lists only --dry-run and --no-index in its Key flags row and does not mention --fail-on-drop; that file was outside this agent's assigned exclusive file scope, so it was deliberately NOT edited. AC#5's 'documented' is currently satisfied by the flag summary in help and the manifest, the module header in src/commands/sync.ts, and the CHANGELOG entry -- not by the reference doc, which is why AC#5 is left unchecked. Separately, and not a defect in this change: the existing Unreleased CHANGELOG bullet for LCLI-479 says 'lore manifest / lore help --json', but lore has no manifest command -- that invocation exits 2 with unknown command. The machine manifest is 'lore help --json', which is where this flag was verified to appear.

AC#5 and AC#7 are deliberately left UNCHECKED, each for a stated reason rather than an oversight. AC#5: the interactions are decided and tested, but docs/reference/cli-surface.md was out of scope, so the reference documentation half is not done -- see the scope-boundary note. AC#7: lint, typecheck and lore check all exit 0, but the suite reports 1 fail plus 1 error from test/ladybug-version-qualification.test.ts's hardcoded worktree-local node_modules path, so 'the test suite passes' is not something this run can claim as evidence -- re-run in the primary checkout and check it there.
finalSummary:
DELIVERED in PR #64, CI run 34900890913 on head 0f18aa5e (the head that also carries origin/dev
merged in, so this was qualified against the tree it lands on, not a stale base).

Implemented by an opum-workflow:implementer under exclusive file scope. I reviewed the DIFF and the
TEST RUN rather than the summary, and re-verified the behaviour myself against a fixture I built.
Everything it claimed held.

WHAT SHIPPED. `lore sync --fail-on-drop` turns the LCLI-485 drop WARNING into a `drift` failure
(exit 6) thrown at the existing warning site -- the last statement before the write phase. Opt-in:
without it, sync still warns, proceeds and exits 0, unchanged. The refusal carries the same count and
the same bounded samples the warning carries, so an unattended runner's captured log is enough to act
on without re-running interactively.

THE CRUX -- "before any write" -- WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT ASSUMED, which is what the task was really
about. A guard that aborts halfway converts a warning into a corrupted tree PLUS a false sense of
protection. Two independent methods:

  1. STATIC: every module on the pre-warning path grepped for write syscalls. Exactly one hit, and it
     is outside the repository -- `bunBacklogSpawn` mkdtempSyncs a throwaway dir under the system
     tmpdir and removes it in a `finally`. Every tracker subcommand `gatherReconciliation` issues is
     a read. This is the specific question the earlier note flagged as UNVERIFIED, and it is now
     answered rather than reasoned about from the function's name.
  2. EMPIRICAL: two tests snapshot every file under the repo root -- docs/, tracker storage, .lore/ --
     as path->bytes and assert byte-identity across the refusal. One also asserts the recording
     GitSpawn.calls is EMPTY, so `sweepTrackerStorage` demonstrably never ran; the other uses a real
     git repository and asserts `rev-list --count HEAD` and `status --porcelain` are unchanged.

EACH SNAPSHOT IS PAIRED WITH A CONTROL: the same fixture run WITHOUT the flag, asserting the tree DOES
change and the commit IS made. A byte-snapshot over a fixture that would never have written anything
proves nothing, and that pairing is the difference between evidence and ceremony.

INDEPENDENTLY RE-VERIFIED BY ME, on a throwaway repo, after a first attempt that proved nothing
(I ran the CLI from lore-cli's own directory, so it synced THIS repo instead of the fixture -- the
"byte-identical" result was measured on a tree nothing had touched). Redone correctly:
`sync --fail-on-drop` exits 6 naming the dropped line, docs/ byte-identical afterwards; the same
fixture with no flag DOES write, so the control holds; `--fail-on-drop --no-index` exits 2.

RESIDUAL GAP, stated rather than papered over: what a third-party quest/backlog binary does inside
its OWN storage while serving a read subcommand is not provable from this repo, and the snapshot
tests use the in-memory fake adapter. That gap is identical for every other lore command.

DECISIONS, each recorded with its reason (AC#6):
 - A FLAG, not a config setting, and not both. The guard changes a run's outcome while sync's
   documented default is "warn and proceed", so a repo-wide setting would make an interactive
   `lore sync` exit 6 for a reason invisible at the call site -- and would then need an inverse flag
   to escape for one run. Two new surfaces, where the unattended callers who asked for this already
   pass flags explicitly in a file where `--fail-on-drop` greps.
 - EXIT `drift` (6), an existing type already in sync's manifest exitCodes. The test asserts against
   `findManifestCommand("sync").exitCodes`, not a literal. `denied`/4 was rejected because the
   read/write seams already return it for EACCES here.
 - `--no-index` + the flag is a USAGE error (exit 2), raised before the bundle loads -- not a silent
   no-op, because the pair reads as protection in a CI file and would provide none.
 - `--dry-run` + the flag still refuses, and the message always says "would drop": a refused run never
   writes, so the warning's indicative "drops" would never be true.

MUTATION-TESTED SEVEN WAYS. The one that matters is M2 -- the guard MOVED to after the write phase
and the sweep -- caught by the tree snapshot, whose diff named docs/index.md and docs/stories/index.md
as created and log.md as rewritten, while the --dry-run test correctly still passed. Also: guard never
fires; exit code swapped; conflict removed; samples dropped from the message; guard ignores the flag
(6 failures, including 3 pre-existing LCLI-485 tests); manifest summary loses "before any write".

AC#5's DOCUMENTATION HALF WAS MINE, not the implementer's. It correctly refused to edit
docs/reference/cli-surface.md because that file was outside the scope it was given, and handed it
back rather than doing it silently. The sync entry listed only --dry-run and --no-index, and its Exit
row named neither 2 nor the new 6 path; both are now accurate.

AC#7 could not be checked by the implementer and it said so instead of claiming green: one test file
ENOENTs in a worktree with no node_modules of its own. Re-run in the primary checkout, it passes.
That is the right failure mode for a delegated agent -- report the anomaly, name the suspected cause,
ask for the verification it cannot perform.

ALSO CAUGHT BY THE IMPLEMENTER, and worth more than its size: the adjacent LCLI-479 changelog entry
named `lore manifest --json`, which IS NOT A COMMAND (it exits 2; the machine manifest is
`lore help --json`). Corrected on dev, with a note on LCLI-479 recording what was true. Nothing in
this repo verifies that a command named in prose exists.

bun run lint 0 (one pre-existing agents.ts warning, untouched), typecheck 0, 3000 pass / 1 skip /
0 fail, lore check 0 errors 0 warnings.
